title: Dal Tadka
subtitle: Yellow lentils with a tempered spice topping
excerpt: Yellow split lentils cooked until soft and creamy, finished with a tadka of cumin, mustard seeds, garlic, and dried chilli fried in butter. A everyday Indian comfort dish that takes less than 40 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal tadka is one of India's most widely eaten everyday dishes. Tadka (also tarka or chaunk) is the technique of blooming whole spices in hot fat and pouring them over the cooked lentils just before serving. The sizzle and spit as the hot oil hits the dal is both technique and theatre. Chana dal (split chickpeas) or toor dal (split pigeon peas) are the most traditional choices; red lentils cook faster and are an easy substitute. The dish is eaten across India with rice, roti, or naan.

content.text: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Red lentils dissolve completely as they cook and require no soaking. The dal should be thick and porridge-like: add water to adjust. The tadka goes on at the end: have the dal ready, prepare the tempering in a separate small pan, and pour it over immediately.

items.preparation: 2 minced for the base, 2 sliced for the tadka

content.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 6 minutes until golden. Add the minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute. Add the ground cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Cook for 30 seconds.

Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes. Add the rinsed lentils and 1 litre of water. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are completely soft and the dal is thick. Season with salt and lemon juice.

Make the tadka: melt the butter in a small pan over high heat until foaming. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 20 seconds. Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes. Cook for 30 seconds until the garlic is golden.
Pour the tadka over the dal immediately. Scatter with fresh coriander. Serve with rice or naan.
